| [CASE-056](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-056.md) | J. B. Phillips's "hearty handshake all round" for Paul's "holy kiss", and Nida's judgement that it keeps the greeting | Phillips renders all five New Testament "holy kiss" directives (Romans 16:16 and four parallels) as handshakes, which changes what the congregation is told to do; Nida (1964, p. 160) holds this up as equivalent effect, and the UBS handbooks call it a brave attempt. The documented case for the necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), on expert judgement rather than reader evidence. | [CASE-059](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-059.md) | Tatiana's letter in Eugene Onegin III: вы to ты and back, lost in Kline and half kept in Spalding | Tatiana's letter to Onegin opens with the formal вы, breaks into the intimate ты at "я твоя", and returns to вы in its last lines; only the pronouns mark the moves. Kline (2009) has "you" throughout, so neither move is in the English; Spalding (1881) switches to "thou" and never returns. A documented candidate for the half of a change of cover in which the source decides a relational question that a rendering makes undecidable. The texts are attested and the loss is visible; native attestation is thin and there is no evidence on English readers. | Active |
| [CASE-062](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-062.md) | Simplified texts for restricted and for full readers: a gain and a loss documented on different texts, documented nulls and a reversal, and a design that tests both on the same renderings | A constructed study, built on documented halves. Simplified texts, made from the source alone, raised comprehension for named restricted readers (adults and adolescents with autism; weaker second-graders), and automatic simplifications lowered it for fluent native readers, but in different studies on different texts. Edited subtitles did not help deaf viewers, and text reduction in captions helped the more proficient readers more. The stipulated design puts both populations on the same renderings, with probe items fixed in advance as answerable from both versions or from the original only. | Active |
| [CASE-063](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-063.md) | The English localization of Ace Attorney: a Japanese courtroom game moved to an alternate Los Angeles, with "textually accurate" set against "emotionally accurate" by its localizer | Capcom's Gyakuten Saiban (2001) became Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney (2005) by moving the courtroom from Japan to Los Angeles. | [CASE-065](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-065.md) | Two satisfaction questions in German and in a back-translated Chinese version: an order effect that reverses across a rendering, with the Clinton–Gore poll as the scale of the 2ε bound | Haberstroh, Oyserman, Schwarz, Kühnen and Ji (2002), Experiment 2, asked German and Chinese students the same two satisfaction questions, in a back-translated Chinese version, in both orders. The part–whole correlation depends on order in the German administration and reverses in the Chinese one, and the authors explain it by a pragmatic mechanism. Only correlations are reported, so the case shows the bound's contrapositive in kind, not in number. Moore's Clinton–Gore poll, held through [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md), supplies the number: an order effect of total variation about 0.095, against a sampling floor of about 0.03 per order at poll sizes, so 2ε is about as large as the effect it would certify. | Active |
| [CASE-066](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-066.md) | Dolly's slip into ты in Anna Karenina I.4, and three English translations that carry it three ways | In Anna Karenina I.4 Dolly says one sentence to Stiva with ты amid вы, and the narrator says so. English has no live T/V pronoun. Dole (1886) keeps the Russian word and glosses it; Garnett (1901) adds "Stiva"; the Maudes (1918) add "our children". The later two add words not in the Russian to carry the relation. Tolstoy himself says вы and its dictionary equivalent vous differ in coldness. A documented instance of the compensation mechanism; the evidence on what readers recover is translators' and the author's, not readers'. | Active |
| [CASE-067](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-067.md) | The reception of Deborah Smith's The Vegetarian: the Booker judges' task, the Korean critics' task, and one critic's two verdicts | Deborah Smith's English version of Han Kang's 채식주의자 won the 2016 Man Booker International Prize, while Korean critics published lists of errors and charged it with embellishment. Each side's task is stated in print: the judges evaluate "the finished English-language work on their own terms", while assessment in Korea "does usually involve comparison". Charse Yun perceives what both sides perceive and gives two verdicts by changing task. Part of the split is access, not weight: some errors are invisible to readers without Korean. | Active |
| [CASE-070](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-070.md) | Voita, Sennrich and Titov's BLEU-tied translation systems that differ on keeping ты or вы across sentences | Two English-to-Russian subtitle translation systems score the same BLEU (32.40 and 32.38, not significantly different). On a contrastive test built from held-out films, which asks whether a system keeps the T or V form of "you" consistent across sentences, one is at chance (50.0%) and the other is right in 81.6% of cases. A documented instance, on a pragmatic distinction, of two realizations equal under a standard probe family and different under an independently built one. An ML paper that neither record holds. | Active |
| [CASE-071](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-071.md) | Kovacs, Deutsch and Freitag's metric bias in MBR decoding: translations a metric selects, that the metric and its neighbours rate better and human raters do not | Minimum Bayes risk and quality-estimation decoding pick, from 128 sampled translations, the one a neural metric scores best. That metric and other neural metrics rate the picks significantly better than greedy decoding; human MQM raters find them no better, and for four system and language-pair combinations significantly worse. [CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)'s result in text, by selection rather than training. The distinction lost is accuracy, not a pragmatic one; a stipulated English-to-Russian ты/вы variant states the design that would make it pragmatic. | Active |
| [CASE-072](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-072.md) | Hafez's "Shirazi Turk" in English: one ungendered beloved rendered as a maid, as God and as a boy | The opening of Hafez's ghazal 3 names a beloved, "that Shirazi Turk", whose sex and nature the Persian leaves open. English forces a choice at the first possessive. Jones (1771) and Bell (1897) make the beloved a maid, Clarke (1891) makes it God, and Davis (2012) makes it a boy, and Davis says in print that his choice is arbitrary. A documented instance of the half of a change of cover in which the rendering decides what the source left open. The disagreement on the source is among translators and scholars; no reader agreement has been measured. | Active |
| [CASE-122](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-122.md) | Warhol's Orange Prince, licensed to Condé Nast in 2016 from a 1981 Goldsmith photograph: the Supreme Court judged the use by its purpose and the dissent by its meaning, and the same cover came out a substitute on one test and a new work on the other | Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith (2023), read in [NOTE-1019](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1019.md). The experts agreed Warhol's silkscreen changed the photograph's meaning, from Prince's private identity to his public image. The majority held that this did not matter for the use at issue: a magazine cover illustrating a story about Prince serves substantially the photograph's own purpose, and new meaning counts only as evidence of a different purpose. The dissent measured what the copier added. One rendering, two measures of what it changed, two verdicts. | Active |
